== Ingredients ==
* 6 [[Cookbook:Egg|eggs]], cold
* 240 [[Cookbook:Milliliter|ml]] (1 [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] + 1 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoon]]) [[Cookbook:Sugar|sugar]]
* 2 ml (½ [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]]) [[Cookbook:Vanilla|vanilla extract]]
* 1 ml ground (¼ teaspoon) [[Cookbook:Nutmeg|nutmeg]]
* 180 ml (¾ cup) [[Cookbook:Brandy|brandy]], cold
* 80 ml (⅓ cup) dark [[Cookbook:Rum|rum]], cold
* 480 ml (2 cups) cups [[Cookbook:Cream|whipping cream]], cold
* 480 ml (2 cups) [[Cookbook:Milk|milk]], cold

== Procedure ==
# [[Cookbook:Whipping|Whip]] the eggs for 2 or 3 minutes with an electric [[Cookbook:Mixer|mixer]] at medium speed until very frothy.
# Gradually [[Cookbook:Beating|beat]] in the sugar, vanilla, and nutmeg.
# Turn the mixer off and stir in the cold brandy, rum, whipping cream, and milk.
# Chill well.
# To serve, sprinkle individual servings with more nutmeg.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* The brandy may be replaced with dark rum.

=== '''Variation I – Extra frothy eggnog''' ===
# [[Cookbook:Separating Eggs|Separate]] egg yolks from egg whites.
# Beat egg yolks first, allowing them to lighten in color.
# Gradually beat in 1 cup sugar'','' vanilla, and nutmeg.
# Turn the mixer off and add liquids.
# Beat egg whites separately, adding the 1 T sugar when peaks form. Continue beating until peaks stiffen.
# Whisk egg whites into the main mixture.
# Chill and serve.

=== '''Variation II – Cooked eggnog''' ===
# Heat milk and cream to [[Cookbook:Scalding|scalding]]. If you wish to make a lower-alcohol version, mix in the liqueurs before scalding to cook out the alcohol.
# [[Cookbook:Tempering|Temper]] the beaten and sweetened egg yolks with the hot milk, before mixing the two.
